was: District of Summerland municipal campground two blocks from Okanagan Lake. 121 sites: 72 with power+water, 49 with water only (no sewer; sani-dump 3 km south). Washrooms, coin showers/laundry, convenience store, pickleball courts, playground. Reservable online. --Claude
note: District of Summerland campground two blocks from Okanagan Lake, whose grassy, shaded sites lie near Eneas Creek (72 have power and water, 49 water only); it has a swing set and six public pickleball courts, and beaches, a spray park and a dog beach are within walking distance.  A sewer service is offered on Wednesdays or Thursdays (ask at the office), and the district's sani-dump is 3 km south.  Wood fires are not allowed; propane fire pits are.  The district gives its 2026 season as May 11 to mid-September. --Claude

was: Oceanside resort on the Kwakiutl First Nation's ancestral land where the Cluxewe River meets Broughton Strait, just N of Port McNeill (Vancouver Island); Indigenous-owned and operated. 137 sites from tent to full/partial hookup RV, incl. oceanfront and woodland sites; showers, laundry, camp store, sani-dump, boat ramp, fish-cleaning station, playground. note: Resort owned and run by the Kwakiutl First Nation on its ancestral land where the Cluxewe River meets Broughton Strait, near Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island, with oceanfront, estuary and woodland sites, a boat ramp, a fish-cleaning station, a playground, barbecue rentals and beachfront cottages.  Generators are not allowed from May 1 to September 30.  A new water treatment plant made the resort's water safe to drink in June 2026. --Claude

was: Four-season private resort on Knouff (Sullivan) Lake, 9608 Knouff Lake Rd, Heffley Creek (~1170 m elev). Drive-in sites with power & water hookups or dry camping, each with picnic table/fire pit; on-site sani-dump, store, showers, laundry; also cabins. RV/tent May-Sep. Reservable via Campspot. --Claude
note: Resort on Knouff Lake, established in 1904 and one of the oldest in B.C., 45 minutes from Kamloops and 30 from Sun Peaks; it holds a North American fly-fishing record for a 17.5 lb dry-fly catch.  RV sites have power and water or no hookups at all, and there is a walk-in tent island, the Hideaway group site for up to five trailers, year-round rustic cabins fitted with cast-iron wood cook stoves, rental trailers, boat rentals and a family beach.  Wi-Fi reaches only the lodge; generators may run from 8 to 10 a.m. and 5 to 7 p.m., and the gate is closed overnight (10 p.m. to 8 a.m. in summer, 9 p.m. to 9 a.m. in winter). --Claude

was: Family-run RV park 5 min west of Lloydminster off Hwy 16; 43 sites with full water/sewer hookups and 15/20/30/50-amp power, pull-throughs for big rigs, plus a few overflow sites; showers, laundry, playground, large grass areas. Available by day/week/month, reservable via Campspot. --Claude
note: Family-run RV park of Ken and Leona Hood, 9 km west of Lloydminster on Highway 16 at Range Road 22, with a playground, a basketball hoop, a rec room of movies, books and board games, off-leash grass areas and central fire pits; it also stores RVs.  Online bookings of the drive-through sites are limited to 4 nights. --Claude

was: Community campground on the Coronation Dam reservoir in the County of Paintearth, east-central Alberta; ~52 sites (50 serviced RV + a tenting area), updated restrooms/token showers, camp kitchen, playground and a boat launch; reservoir stocked with trout and walleye. Open May 1-Sept 30, reservable via Campspot. --Claude
note: Town of Coronation campground on the Coronation Dam reservoir, with newly built washrooms, group camping areas, a new playground and a camp kitchen to rent.  The reservoir holds rainbow trout and northern pike and has a launch for small fishing boats (12-volt electric motors only). --Claude
